sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 descriptive bibliography for bulu1251 (19 refs) and WALS languages file (buw: Bulu; sources Alexandre 1966, Bates 1904; no values for stress chapters 14A-17A)
sources.note: WALS codes Bulu only for 27A, 86A, 101A, 143A/E/F/G — no stress-chapter value, so no secondary-database stress claim exists. Glottolog lists Alexandre 1955/1966, Abomo-Maurin 2006, Bates 1904/1926, Good 1936, von Hagen 1914, Wilkinson 1975, Ndi 2001 (pure.mpg.de item_403449, HTTP 403), Alexandre 1962 JAL article.

sources.citation: Krug, Adolph N. 1912. Bulu tales from Kamerun, West Africa. Journal of American Folklore 25: 106-124; Schwab, George. 1914. Bulu folk-tales. JAF 27: 266-288; [Jacob, Hermann]. 1895. Bikange bi Bulu. 24 pp.
sources.note: Texts/tales only; grep for accent/stress/tone/pronunciation returned nothing relevant.

sources.citation: Clem, Emily. 2014. The interaction of lexical and grammatical tone in the Bulu verb system. Honors thesis, Department of Linguistics, The Ohio State University (kb.osu.edu handle 1811/59932).
sources.note: §1.1.2 Tone (p. 4): 'The language makes use of two phonological tone levels, high (H) and low (L). Surface tones can also include rising and falling tones... downstep'. No mention of stress or accent anywhere. Speaker from the Sangmélima area.

sources.citation: Yukawa, Yasutoshi. 1992. A tonological study of Bulu verbs. In: Studies in Cameroonian and Zairean languages (Bantu Linguistics 3), 67-93. Tokyo: ILCAA. (TUFS repository record 11512, hdl 10108/93057)
sources.note: Introduction pp. 67-68 gives consonant/vowel inventories and marks high, rising and falling tone (low unmarked); whole paper is verb tonology. No mention of stress or accent (scanned of 27 image-only pages grepped for stress/accent/prominence: no hits). Informant born Ebolowa 1960.

sources.citation: Ze Amvela, Etienne & S. M. Eno Belinga. 1978. Caractéristiques linguistiques du Bulu utilisé dans l'épopée orale du Mvet. Journal des Africanistes 48(2): 121-132.
sources.note: Persée page text (PDF endpoint 403): footnote 1 'le bulu distingue trois tons principaux : un haut ( ´), un moyen ( ¯), et un bas ( `)'. Nothing on stress in the visible text.

sources.citation: Wilkinson, Robert W. 1975. The phonemic status of mid tone in Ebolowa Bulu. Proceedings of the Sixth Conference on African Linguistics, OSU Working Papers in Linguistics 20: 75-86.
sources.note: Tonology only: argues for three tonemes /L M H/ in Ebolowa Bulu (vs Alexandre 1962/1966 two-tone analysis); the word 'stress' appears once, citing floating stresses in Terena (p. 77). Nothing on Bulu word stress.

sources.citation: Alexandre, Pierre & Jacques Binet. 1958. Le groupe dit Pahouin (Fang - Boulou - Beti). Paris: PUF / IAI. Chapter 'La langue' (HRAF FH9 microfiche scanned).
sources.note: 'Au point de vue phonétique, la caractéristique la plus importante du groupe est sans doute l'emploi de tons... Bates et Johnson reconnaissent cinq tons, plus le glissando du négatif. Bertaut, après les auteurs allemands, distingue deux tons fondamentaux — haut et bas — deux tons dérivés — ascendant et descendant — et un ton moyen'; rhythm said to matter in drum messages. No statement on word stress (scanned patchy).

sources.citation: [Jeffreys, M. D. W.] 1945. Some historical notes on African tone languages. African Studies 4(3): 135-146 (author inferred from self-citations).
sources.note: Quotes Bates 1904 Handbook of Bulu p. 7 verbatim on tone: 'Certain words in Bulu are always spoken in a higher tone than that of ordinary speech, and others in a lower tone than ordinary. This often affords in speaking a means of distinguishing between homonyms... the common word mot, person, is always spoken in a low tone'; also cites Bates 1926 p. 5. No word-stress statement; second-hand access to Bates.
